incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16 (OBCA), ss. 4-10 (incorporation and articles), s. 17 (registered office), s. 22 (share rights), ss. 98, 113 (directors and officers), s. 140 (corporate records); prescribed forms under O. Reg. 62/18.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch; administered through ServiceOntario via the Ontario Business Registry (www.ontario.ca/ontario-business-registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Article of Incorporation (Ontario Form 1, Incorporation Application) filed online with the Ontario Business Registry; the Director under the OBCA issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the OBCA; the corporation may incorporate with nil issued capital and issue shares for such consideration as the directors determine. No escrow account or capital trust arrangement is mandated at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED AS THE FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CORPORATION NAME]: (1) The incorporator's subscription for 100 common shares is accepted; the shares shall be issued as fully paid and non-assessable, and a share certificate shall be delivered to the subscriber; (2) The registered office of the Corporation shall be maintained at [registered municipal address in Ontario], where the statutory records and corporate minute book shall be kept; (3) The following officers are appointed to hold office until the next annual shareholders' meeting: President, Secretary, and Treasurer; and (4) The appointed officers are authorized to open corporate and merchant settlement accounts and to complete the Canada Revenue Agency Business Number registration. This resolution is effective immediately upon incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry via ServiceOntario; NUANS search system administered by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names through the Ontario Business Registry online portal or an authorized service provider; pay the search fee to obtain a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report. The report identifies conflicting existing corporate names and trademarks. If the proposed name is not distinguishable under the OBCA Name Regulation, select an alternate name. As an alternative, a numbered corporation may be formed by direct filing without a name search.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names (up to three, including distinctive element)
NUANS search request and payment authorization
Applicant confirmation of availability of the name for use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, re-run the NUANS search against an alternate name; if a conflict exists with a consenting name holder, file a letter of consent from that holder. Alternatively, adopt a numbered corporation (e.g., 123456789 Ontario Inc.) and register a trade name under the Business Names Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.11.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and File Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Director under the OBCA; Ontario Business Registry (ServiceOntario).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Incorporation Application (Ontario Form 1) setting out the corporate name or numbered name, share structure (authorized classes, voting rights, transfer restrictions), number of first directors (minimum one), the municipal address of the registered office in Ontario, and the names and residential/municipal addresses of the incorporator and first directors. Attach the NUANS report for a name-based incorporation, and remit the CAD $300 filing fee by credit card. The Registry reviews priority filings and issues the Certificate of Incorporation; corporate existence commences on the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 Articles of Incorporation
NUANS report (for named corporations)
Consent of each first director to act
Registered office municipal address in Ontario (P.O. Box not acceptable)
Filing fee payment authorization (CAD $300)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect or query notice, file a corrected resubmission under OBCA s. 9 within the stated period; if the articles are already accepted, apply to the Director for a letter of correction or for a Certificate of Amendment under s. 169. Minor omissions may be cured by an affidavit of correction and, if a name is refused, by filing a numbered name variation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Director under the OBCA; Ontario Business Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance of the Articles, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Confirm that the registered office address and the first directors shown in the Articles are accurate and current. Record the certificate date and Ontario Corporation Number in the corporate records. If the registered office is not the principal place of business, appoint the registered office as the service-of-process address and notify the Registry of any subsequent change using Form 3 (Notice of Change).
required_dossiers: Issued Certificate of Incorporation
Endorsed copy of Articles of Incorporation
Ontario Corporation Number confirmation
Registered office address verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the service standard, contact the Ontario Business Registry contact centre for status; if address or director information was misstated, file a Form 3 Notice of Change with corrective details or apply for a certificate of correction under OBCA s. 9.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organizational Meeting and Corporate Governance Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate secretary and directors (internal corporate governance; no government filing required).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or execute the pro-forma first board resolution in writing to record: acceptance of the subscriber's share issuance, designation of the registered office, appointment of officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer), approval of share certificates, adoption of Bylaw No. 1 (model bylaw) if desired, selection of fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31), opening of banking and payment-rail accounts (Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex), and appointment of authorized signatories. Place all governing documents in the corporate minute book, including the Articles, Certificate, consents of directors, share register, transfer register, and the resolutions.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Written consents of directors to act
Bylaw No. 1 (adopted model bylaw)
Share certificate stock and share register
Minute book and corporate records filing system
Authorized signatory list for banking and payment accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an action was taken without a valid resolution, ratify the action by a subsequently passed ordinary resolution under the OBCA; defects in unanimous written resolutions may be cured by the signed consent of all directors; maintain a supplemental recorded resolution to correct omissions in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Business Registration Online portal (bro.cra-arc.gc.ca).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online registration for a nine-digit Business Number (BN) using the Ontario incorporation certificate number and corporate legal name. Confirm the appropriate program accounts: GST/HST (e.g., for online sales; zero-rated goods may render the account optional, but registration allows input tax credit claims), payroll account (once employees are hired), and the corporate income tax account. Provide registered office address, fiscal year-end, director/officer information, and North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS 454110) for internet retail. Retain the CRA confirmation letter for Amazon marketplace and payment-rail compliance.
required_dossiers: Ontario Certificate of Incorporation and Ontario Corporation Number
Registered office and mailing address
Full names and addresses of directors/officers
Expected fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31)
Bank account details for CRA direct deposit (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA issues a compliance query or the BN is incorrect, contact the CRA Business Enquiries line (1-800-959-5525) or submit Form RC139A (Request for Update of Information); if the account registration is incomplete, amend the registration online before filing the first return. Retroactive GST/HST registration may be permitted under the Excise Tax Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licensing, Zoning, and Occupational Clearance Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal licensing and building division (e.g., City of Toronto Municipal Licensing & Standards); local fire department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the municipality imposes a general business licence or home-occupation permit for a virtual/online retailer. For an Amazon FBA e-commerce operation with no public storefront and no on-site manufacturing, no municipal operating licence is typically mandated. If a home office or small storage area is used, apply for a Home Occupation Permit or obtain a zoning certificate confirming the use is permitted. For any premises with employees, verify compliance with the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07), obtain property standards clearance, and confirm compliance with the Workplace Safety and Insurance Act, 1997 (WSIB registration once payroll exists).
required_dossiers: Copy of Certificate of Incorporation
CRA Business Number confirmation
Lease, ownership deed, or signed consent of landlord
Zoning confirmation or Home Occupation Permit application
Fire safety plan (if office or storage occupancy)
WSIB clearance or exemption confirmation (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning does not permit the activity, apply for a Minor Variance before the municipal Committee of Adjustment or select a compliant premises; if a fire safety deficiency is identified, submit a corrective Fire Safety Plan to the local Fire Marshal and obtain re-inspection; appeal any licensing refusal through the Municipal Licensing and Standards Committee or the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal as available.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None for pure e-commerce resale under ISIC 4791 (Internet marketplace FBA store). If a physical warehouse or fulfillment operation is established in Ontario, the Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development exercises occupational health and safety jurisdiction, and the local building department serves as the industrial permitting authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for a pure online store. No operating or manufacturing permit is required by the Ontario Government for an Amazon FBA general merchandise reseller; a municipal Home Occupation Permit may be required for a home-based office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP) under the Environmental Assessment Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.18 and the Environmental Protection Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.19.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. Internet retail (ISIC 4791) is not listed as an undertaking requiring environmental assessment under O. Reg. 116/01; no EIA registration, screening, or approval is triggered by virtual, non-manufacturing operations. Only a minor exemption for a local warehouse or distribution centre may require evaluation if an Environmental Compliance Approval is needed for equipment such as large HVAC systems.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for pure cloud-based FBA sales. If the corporation operates a local storage facility: wastewater must meet municipal sewer-use bylaw and Ontario Sewer/Sewage Works standards under O. Reg. 403/04; air emissions, including VOCs and nitrogen oxides, are subject to concentration limits under O. Reg. 419/05; solid waste and recycling must comply with O. Reg. 347/90 and applicable extended producer responsibility programs for packaging and waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: compliance with the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07) is mandatory for any occupied office or storage space, including portable extinguishers, fire separation, and evacuation plans. Structural load inspections are required only if racking, mezzanines, or professional storage equipment is installed; in such cases Part 4 of the Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 332/12) applies. Workplace clearance: the corporation must register with the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) once it hires employees and maintain proof of compliance; employment of owners without payroll does not trigger WSIB coverage or a certificate requirement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal at canada.ca and My Business Account (MBD). Import/export customs control is administered by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) via eManifest/ACROSS; Ontario corporate income tax is administered by the CRA on behalf of Ontario under the Federal–Provincial Tax Collection Agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate as an Ontario Business Corporation under the OBCA or a federal corporation under the CBCA (extra-provincial registration in Ontario). 2. Apply for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) simultaneously electing GST/HST program account (RT), payroll (RP), and import/export (RM) accounts. 3. The GST/HST registration number is the BN suffixed with 'RT0001'; a separate Ontario tax registration is not required because Ontario participates in the federal HST system and Ontario corporate tax collection. 4. Non-resident corporations may apply using Form RC1 or BRO via an authorized representative, submitting foreign certificate of incorporation, director/officer details, and a Canadian agent for service. 5. Register with CBSA for an importer/exporter account requiring an RM program account and customs surety bond (usually CAD 25,000 for non-residents; Canadian-controlled importers of record may post a specified security).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Canadian business corporation is an independent taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act; no default tax-transparent treatment applies to a corporation. Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) may access the small business deduction (Ontario combined rate of 12.2% on active business income up to CAD 500,000) versus 26.5% general corporate rate; the federal dividend tax credit partially integrates distributions but does not alter entity-level taxation. Territorial scope: Canadian-resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income with foreign tax credits; domestic sales and Ontario HST apply within the provincial HST regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a US-style check-the-box regime. Available elections and designations: (a) ETA s. 156 election for nil consideration between related registrants; (b) ETA Quick Method of Accounting for registrants with taxable supplies under CAD 400,000 (CAD 800,000 for public service bodies); (c) ETA simplified annual GST/HST filing election; (d) Income Tax Act s. 256(1) agreement allocating the small business deduction limit among associated CCPCs; (e) s. 85(1) rollover elections on qualifying transfers (relevant to migration of inventory/intangibles); (f) ETA s. 179 election designating an agent or consignee status for cross-border marketplace supply chain; (g) ETA Schedule VI certifications for zero-rated export supplies; (h) formal deemed-supplier arrangement under the 2021 cross-border e-commerce framework where a marketplace platform (Amazon.ca) collects and remits GST/HST on behalf of an unregistered non-resident fulfilment vendor.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — Federal GST at 5% combined with Ontario provincial PST through the harmonized system at 13%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — GST/HST registration is mandatory once the supplier's worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or over the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 240; small supplier threshold). Amazon FBA operators typically exceed this threshold upon operating commencement and are advised to register immediately; non-resident fulfilment vendors selling inventory stored in Canadian fulfilment centres are deemed to carry on business in Canada and cannot rely on small-supplier status where the marketplace platform acts as deemed supplier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or government digital stamping regime is operational in Canada. A registrant must issue a sales invoice or simplified receipt containing prescribed information: supplier name, BN and GST/HST registration number, invoice date, invoice number, a description of the goods/services, tax payable, and the status of zero-rated/exempt supplies (ETA s. 223). Electronic invoicing is expressly permitted and the Pan-Canadian e-Invoicing program (Peppol network) is being phased in voluntarily from 2024–2025. Cross-border movements through CBSA require eManifest/ACI data (arrival certification) and, for exports, the B13A declaration or low-value in-transit exemption; Amazon Seller Central acts as the primary transaction reconciliation portal and no API-based fiscal clearance is currently mandated for B2C marketplace invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 5–6 where the supplier exports, or causes the export of, the tangible personal property by delivery to the purchaser or a common carrier for shipment outside Canada within a reasonable time (normally 60–90 days), and documentation proving export is retained. Services: zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 when supplied to a non-resident provided the service is not performed wholly in Canada and does not relate to real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of supply; digital marketplace and software-as-a-service fees to non-residents qualify with proper contracts and billing records. Amazon FBA-specific: sales shipped to Canadian customers through Amazon.ca fulfilment centres are taxable at 13% HST in Ontario; export sales made from Canadian inventory through Amazon cross-border channels (US destinations) qualify for 0% GST/HST where title passes abroad, goods are physically exported by the FBA export carrier, and the corresponding export documentation is retained. Imported inventory entering Ontario via FBA is subject to 13% HST at importation, recoverable as an input tax credit (ITC) by the GST/HST registrant.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Export Declaration (or qualified in-transit exemption for low-value shipments) with CBSA approval and unique transaction number
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the exported goods, quantities, and stated 0% GST/HST classification
Transport document evidencing departure from Canada: Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or carrier trailer manifest issued by the common carrier
CBSA/ACROSS declaration report or licensed customs broker certificate confirming the date and port of export
Bank receipt, SWIFT confirmation, or Inward Remittance Certificate equivalent evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency export proceeds in the Canadian entity's account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA's Export Verification Program and CBSA joint audits scrutinize e-commerce exporters for documented physical export, revenue recognition, and FX inflow. Where zero-rating documentation is deficient, CRA will claw back the 0% treatment and reassess the full supply at 13% HST, with arrears interest at the prescribed rate (currently 7%–9% per annum compound) from the date of the original return plus a penalty under ETA s. 280(1) equal to 6% of any unremitted net tax amounts. Knowingly making false statements, omitting material information, or claiming fraudulent export refunds attracts a s. 285(1) penalty of CAD 250 or 25% of the net tax, and under s. 285(1.2) a 50% misrepresentation penalty on misstated credits; criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327(1)(a) and Criminal Code s. 380 can result in imprisonment of 5–14 years. Fraudulent refund attempts extend the normal four-year reassessment period to 10 years or indefinitely; CRA may also issue a requirements notice to Amazon to withhold and remit marketplace disbursements for the settling of assessed GST/HST liabilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority, operating the Canadian-dollar free-float and general monetary policy pursuant to the Bank of Canada Act. Foreign exchange policy and the official Exchange Fund Account are administered by the Minister of Finance (Department of Finance Canada) under the Currency Act. Prudential supervision of Schedule I banks is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) enforces the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada has no specialized foreign-exchange control bureau; the Foreign Exchange Control Board was dissolved in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility under a free-floating exchange rate; Canada has observed IMF Article VIII obligations since 1952. No exchange licensing, approval, quotas, or surrender requirements apply to residents or non-residents. Dividends, branch remittances, interest, and royalties are freely transferable abroad, subject only to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (statutory 25%; treaty-reduced rates typically 5% to 15% for direct dividends, and 0% to 15% for interest and royalties under the Canada-US, Canada-China, and Canada-Hong Kong tax treaties) and to money-laundering reporting thresholds. Capital injections and loan repayments are unrestricted. FINTRAC requires financial institutions to report inbound and outbound electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more per transaction or per 24-hour series; this is a compliance reporting obligation, not a convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export-proceeds surrender or conversion obligation exists in Canada. An exporter may retain, transfer, or convert foreign currency freely in domestic or offshore accounts. Foreign-currency accounting and CAD-equivalent translation (including the functional-currency election on Form T1133 under section 261 of the Income Tax Act) apply only for tax reporting purposes. Practical reporting duties: the settlement bank files FINTRAC EFT reports for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, and the exporter must retain underlying trade documentation to evidence economic substance. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD) and USD Foreign-Currency Account; Capital Escrow sub-account
Operational Account (CAD); USD Foreign-Currency Banking account
Operational Account (CAD/USD); strengthened trade-finance desk and Asian-corridor clearing for FBA inventory purchases
Operational Account; Capital Escrow / Equity Subscription account
Operational Account (CAD); cross-border e-commerce treasury solutions less developed in Ontario

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for operational collection and disbursement flows; LOW for statutory capital escrow and regulated treasury purposes. Airwallex Canada, Inc. holds a FINTRAC money-service-business registration and offers multi-currency (CAD, USD, EUR, CNH) transaction accounts with domestic Canadian clearing through partner Schedule I banks; it is not a deposit-taking institution, so the primary capital escrow account, Part XIII withholding mechanics, and OSFI-supervised liquidity should remain with a Big-Six bank. Stripe Canada, Ltd. (FINTRAC-registered) acts as a merchant acquirer and payout processor suitable for Amazon marketplace receivables, but does not provide interbank FX dealing, derivative credit lines, or SWIFT trade disbursement services. Legal constraint: a foreign EU or UK FCA-licensed EMI cannot passport into Canada; it must obtain a Canadian money-services-business registration, operate through an OSFI-authorized foreign bank branch (Schedule III), or act only as a payment facilitator with no deposit-taking. Ontario's Consumer Protection Act and the Money Transfer Act, 2016 (Ontario) impose applicable money-transfer registration requirements on remittance activities; the standard Airwallex and Stripe models satisfy these via FINTRAC registration and partnership with licensed Canadian deposit-takers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement that directors of a low-risk ISIC 4791 e-commerce operating corporation appear physically at a bank branch; however, each Schedule I bank must complete customer identification and verification. Remote digital onboarding is accepted by RBC, TD, CIBC, and BMO for corporations with at least one Canadian-resident director or officer: the process requires a live video KYC interview, digital verification of government-issued photo ID, and delivery of a notarized corporate resolution and authorized-signatory list. Under the Ontario Business Corporations Act (OBCA), at least one director must be resident Canadian, and under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) at least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians; therefore the resident Canadian director should attend the onboarding session in person or by high-assurance video-notary. Non-resident directors execute a notarized signature book, and foreign public documents carry a Hague Apostille where applicable; bare notarization is accepted for non-public corporate documents. The KYC interview mandate is satisfied by at least one physical or remotely notarized interview per entity, supplemented by apostilled or notarized corporate records. Power-of-attorney-only account structures for the marketplace subsidiary are discouraged.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or delayed beneficial-ownership disclosure: the foreign parent chain contains offshore intermediate holding companies, or the ultimate beneficial owner disclosure is incomplete at the corporate registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBCA or OBCA articles of incorporation; updated register of individuals with significant control (ISC) or Ontario registry search; full organizational chart covering each holding layer; beneficial-ownership declaration executed by each natural person holding 25% or more; legal opinion confirming no bearer shares or nominee arrangements and identifying all ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch: rapid inbound flows from Amazon marketplace settlements exceed the declared capital base and prompt a suspicious-transaction assessment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of Amazon seller-central settlement and payout reports; Stripe or other gateway transaction summaries; accountant's comfort letter confirming the e-commerce revenue model; inbound wire statements cross-referenced to marketplace remitter identifiers; management accounts evidencing marketplace net margin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: China-corridor supplier payments for FBA inventory restocking are treated as high risk due to transfers-pricing concerns, IP risk, or sanctions screening hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Triangular trade file comprising purchase orders, supplier invoices with HS codes, bills of lading, customs broker entries (CBSA import records), freight forwarder invoices, and Amazon FBA inbound shipment manifests; arm's-length pricing evidence benchmarked against comparable online retail costs; sanctions screening report (LexisNexis or Refinitiv) demonstrating no restricted-party match.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid credit profile on a newly incorporated company with high transaction velocity and no filed financial statements, creating a shell-treasury red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month rolling business plan with FBA storage-fee projections and inventory-turnover analysis; marketplace account verification details; commercial lease or utility agreement at the registered office; evidence of physical product operations such as supplier factory records or receiving reports; reviewed financial statements as soon as available; trade references from logistics providers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons among ultimate beneficial owners or signatories, triggering automatic escalation to the bank's PEP advisory unit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete PEP declarations on the bank's prescribed forms; notarized source-of-wealth memorandum; independent public-registry search evidencing no enforcement history; legal opinion from a licensed Canadian lawyer confirming that political exposure does not impair the entity; if a PEP is confirmed, an enhanced monitoring plan and a board-signed risk-mitigation letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound equity from the non-resident shareholder via SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian operating account, with remittance narrative stating: SHARE CAPITAL INJECTION - [legal entity name] - Reference [board resolution number]. Canada does not maintain a statutory central-bank purpose-code list; the receiving bank maps the transaction to an internal capital-flow category for FINTRAC EFT reporting, which is mandatory for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. The receiving bank will request: (1) a board resolution authorizing share issuance and account signatories; (2) the share subscription agreement; (3) evidence of the shareholder's source of funds (originator bank statement and parent tax records); (4) an updated share register; and (5) for subscriptions exceeding CAD 100,000 in cost, a determination of Form T1135 foreign-property reporting exposure for the Canadian company. Equity subscriptions are not subject to Part XIII withholding tax. FX conversion should be executed at a competitive dealing desk rate, or the inbound USD or CNH should be parked in a linked foreign-currency account to avoid forced conversion. The Capital Escrow classification at a Schedule I bank quarantines the initial paid-in capital until the bank's KYC and sanctions acceptance is complete, after which funds are released to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Amazon marketplace payouts settle in CAD through the Canadian Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) as direct deposits, or into an Airwallex virtual account on the same domestic rail; USD-denominated Amazon.com payouts should land in a Canadian USD settlement account to avoid forced conversion. Supplier payments to the People's Republic of China are executed by SWIFT MT103 with field 50K remittance information citing the underlying purchase order and contract, routed over SWIFT gpi for tracking through correspondent banks (typically HSBC, Standard Chartered, J.P. Morgan, or a Bank of China Canadian correspondent); CNY settlement may use CIPS-linked correspondent clearing where the beneficiary bank is a CIPS member. Large inventory purchases above USD 250,000 equivalent use an irrevocable confirmed commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700; UCP600 rules) issued by the Canadian bank, with 120-day usance and Incoterms 2020 (FOB or CIP) to provide documentary control. Payroll and Canada Revenue Agency remittances flow through ACSS EFT and the CRA payroll remittance rail; contractor payments route through EFT (T4A basis). FX payment optimization requires settling USD-to-CNH exposure via offshore CNH swaps or converting natural USD revenue at the bank's dealing desk only when surplus USD remains after supplier payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, GBP/CAD; tenors typically up to 24 months) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's FX master agreement, permitted for genuine commercial hedging of Amazon settlement revenue and supplier payables.
FX swaps between CAD and USD (spot against forward) for liquidity timing mismatches between Amazon settlement cycles and inventory payable dates, subject to bank Treasury dealer and credit approval.
Cross-currency swaps (ISDA/CSA governed) for long-dated USD/CAD or EUR/CAD hedging of material capex or loan re-denomination, requiring an executed ISDA Master Agreement and credit support annex.
Zero-cost FX collar strategies (purchase of a cap funded by the sale of a floor) and vanilla FX options, permitted when a documented commercial exposure exists and board approval is recorded.

CME-listed USD/CAD and EUR/CAD futures and exchange-traded options as margin-efficient alternatives that require no bank derivative credit line; permitted for commercial hedgers under Canadian commodity futures rules.

Offshore-deliverable CNH forwards and CNH/CAD swaps (Hong Kong CNH market) layered onto a USD/CAD forward to synthesize a fully hedged CNY landed cost for China-sourced FBA inventory; onshore CNY NDFs against CAD are unnecessary because CAD is fully convertible, but CNH NDF overlays remain permissible where the underlying trade flow is documented.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Annual Return (OBCA s. 113; Corporations Information Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Business Registry, ServiceOntario (Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years permits ministerial notice leading to charter revocation and administrative dissolution under OBCA s. 240; directors and shareholders may be jointly and severally liable for statutory debts under OBCA s. 243.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA s. 263) for federally incorporated entities active in Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Director to publish a notice; if cause is not shown within 120 days, the corporation may be dissolved under CBCA s. 212; post-dissolution director and shareholder liability applies to corporate obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Income Tax Act s. 150(1))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after taxation year end; two-month deadline for non-CCPCs or corporations with taxable capital exceeding CAD 15 million
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; 10% repeated-failure penalty; daily compounding prescribed-rate interest; willful evasion may be prosecuted under Income Tax Act s. 239.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue threshold triggers a mandatory audit for a private OBCA/CBCA corporation. Every distributing (public) corporation must appoint an auditor; a non-distributing private corporation is exempt if all shareholders unanimously resolve in writing to waive the audit (OBCA s. 148(2); CBCA s. 163(2)). Audit becomes compulsory when requested by a shareholder, required by the articles or a unanimous shareholder agreement, or mandated for regulated sectors.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private companies may elect Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); publicly accountable enterprises must apply IFRS. Financial statements must be prepared on a consistent GAAP basis and filed with the T2 corporate return; CRA requires books and records in English or French.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Conduct an annual review of the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) as of each fiscal year end; update the register within 15 days of any transfer or change in significant control (direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more of voting shares or de facto control) per CBCA s. 21.1 and Ontario ISC requirements; confirm director names, addresses, and share structure when filing the Ontario/Federal Annual Return; maintain reasonable-steps documentation and keep the register at the registered office; no public UBO filing applies to private Ontario corporations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,400–13,000 (CAD 6,000–18,000) for a full statutory audit; review engagement approximately USD 1,500–5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined ordinary rate (Federal Part I 15% + Ontario general 11.5%); Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business rate 12.2% (Federal 9% + Ontario 3.2%) on the first CA$500,000 of qualifying active business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for e-commerce distribution. Available incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) for qualifying CCPCs only; Federal Manufacturing and Processing (M&P) reduced rate of 13% where applicable; SR&ED investment tax credits; Ontario Innovation Tax Credit; 10-year carryforward of charitable donations and indefinite carryforward of net capital losses; non-capital losses carried back 3 years and forward 20 years

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) e-filed via CRA NETFILE and CRA My Business Account; Ontario corporate tax schedules are embedded in the T2 package under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations may elect an alternative fiscal year of 52/53 weeks under s. 249.1 ITA
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., a 31-Dec-2025 year-end is due 30-Jun-2026); tax balance due date is 2 months after fiscal year-end (3 months for a qualifying CCPC); no extension of time is granted for the T2 filing date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales revenue from Amazon FBA marketplace operations less returns, allowances, and discounts; reconciled to Amazon Seller Central settlement reports
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide FBA sales proceeds recognized under IFRS 15/ASPE 3400; intercompany purchases from non-arm's-length foreign suppliers must be booked at arm's-length fair value and supported by transfer-pricing documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed under s. 3 ITA: business income after s. 247 transfer-pricing adjustments, s. 18 deductibility rules, and application of the loss-ordering rules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible items (unceased meals/gifts 50%, fines, reserves) and adjust for transfer-pricing upward revaluations; foreign exchange gains/losses are translated using the Bank of Canada annual average rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes basic federal Part I tax at the general rate of 15% before deductions and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A wholly foreign-owned FBA corporation is not a CCPC and therefore cannot claim the Small Business Deduction; only the M&P deduction, investment tax credits, and non-refundable credits apply

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocates Ontario taxable income using the permanent-establishment formula (Ontario salaries and gross revenue relative to Canadian totals) and applies the Ontario general rate of 11.5%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amazon FBA warehouses located in Ontario may create a permanent establishment of the Ontario corporation; all sales sourced to that PE must be included in the Ontario allocation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax under s. 163(2); failure to file information schedules CA$25 per day per form up to CA$2,500; general failure-to-file fine under s. 238(1) of CA$1,000 to CA$25,000; CRA prescribed-rate interest compounded daily on any arrears
